summary: You present clear, scenario-specific architecture reasoning, especially in Questions 2 and 4, and your communication meets the rubric’s highest level. To strengthen the work further, make the availability response measurable, correct the end-to-end calculation in Question 3(c), explain CAP accurately, and include a negative consequence in your ADR.
next_steps: In Question 1, replace “stay up most of the time” with a measurable availability target, such as a specified percentage over a stated period, and check that each scenario includes all six parts.

In Question 3(c), distinguish the redundant payment-provider availability from end-to-end order-placement availability; include all required components and show the resulting monthly downtime. In Question 5, explain that during a network partition, consistency and availability must be traded off, then connect each choice to its technique.

In Question 6, add a specific negative consequence of the queue decision, such as added operational complexity or delayed notifications. State any assumptions explicitly, as required by the task. Retain the scenario-specific trade-offs in Question 2 and the outage application and tuning consideration in Question 4.

criteria.C1: In Question 1, you chose relevant attributes and gave a measurable performance response measure. Make “stay up most of the time” measurable to meet the next level’s response-measure requirement.
criteria.C2: In Question 2, your modular-monolith recommendation is grounded in the five-person team and existing bottleneck, and you acknowledge a downside. Keep these scenario-specific trade-offs clear.
criteria.C3: In Question 3, parts (a) and (b) are correct. In part (c), you report payment-provider availability as end-to-end availability; include all required components and recalculate the result and downtime.
criteria.C4: In Question 4, you explain and apply the Circuit Breaker to the provider outage, and give a threshold and time window as tuning considerations. This is a strong, complete response.
criteria.C5: In Question 5, your menu-cache choice and payment idempotency key are concrete. Correct the CAP explanation: under a partition, consistency and availability trade off; partition tolerance is not the option to give up.
criteria.C6: In Question 6, your Context, Decision and positive consequences are specific to the scenario. Add at least one negative consequence of the queue decision to complete the ADR.
criteria.C7: Your headings, concise answers and IEEE-style numbered citations meet the communication requirements. Also state any assumptions explicitly, as the task requires.
